analyst_view.overall: Ferencvaros are 3rd with four wins from four in Europe, including 2-0 at AC Milan, and coach Balazs Borbely says a top-eight finish would matter both in sport and financially; Celje are 25th with 4 points but have won five in a row in all competitions. Ferencvaros lost 3-1 at home to Gyor (ETO) on Saturday and are without Bamidele Yusuf (banned after his red in Milan) and Bence Otvos; the numbers count both, about -17% on Ferencvaros's goals for Yusuf. Lenny Joseph came back late from Haiti duty and Borbely kept his attacking line-up secret; Celje report no new absences, with Svit Seslar and Armandas Kucys fit. Celje coach Zoran Zeljkovic says his side's strength is technique rather than physique and Borbely expects them to keep the ball, in cold weather in Budapest. Italian referee Simone Sozza (about 4.1 cards a game) is in charge and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and already take a big slice off Ferencvaros for Yusuf's ban, with Joseph or Zachariassen likely to lead the line. Celje arrive on five straight wins but have scored only 5 in four European games, and today's press conferences brought no new absences, so I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, already a little higher because Celje have conceded 43 corners in their last six. Ferencvaros should have more of the ball at home, as the 5.4 to 3.9 split shows, while Celje want to pass through rather than go long, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already trimmed for both sides' calm recent card counts and set by referee Simone Sozza's average record (4.1 a game in 52 games). Both coaches expect a footballing game rather than a physical one, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.3 shots, with Celje's quieter recent shooting (49 in six) already taking 11% off their side. Ferencvaros are close to full strength apart from Yusuf and Otvos, both counted, and Celje report no new injuries, so I stay at 25.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, already raised for Ferencvaros's sharp recent finishing (31 on target in six). Joseph, back late from international duty, may not be at his best, but Borbely says he is not out of form, so this is too small to move and I stay at 9.6.
